dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are concerned about an itchy rash on both of your arms; when did you first notice this appearing?
Hi, Dr. Agent. I first noticed this rash about five months ago, and it just hasn't gone away since then. It gets a bit worse sometimes, but it’s always itchy and uncomfortable on both my arms.
Can you describe what the rash looks like—is it dry, scaly, or does it have any bumps or blisters? Also, do you have a history of asthma, hay fever, or similar skin issues in your family?

The skin looks quite dry and thick, almost like it's scaly in the areas where I've been scratching it the most. I don't recall having asthma or hay fever, but I do remember my mother saying I had some skin issues as a very small child.

Where exactly on your arms is the rash located, such as the insides of your elbows or the outer surfaces? Also, have you noticed anything that makes the itching worse, like certain soaps, heat, or stress? 

REQUEST TEST: Physical_Examination

RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), Blood Pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart Rate 76 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Skin Examination: Bilateral erythematous, scaly, and crusted lesions localized to the upper extremities. Lesions are slightly raised and rough to touch; no warmth or induration noted upon palpation.
Does the rash primarily affect the creases of your elbows, and have you noticed it anywhere else on your body like your legs or neck? Also, have you started using any new soaps
It's mostly right in the folds of my elbows, though it does spread a bit up and down my arms too. I haven't seen it on my legs or neck lately, and I haven't changed my soaps or detergents at all.
Have you tried any over-the-counter treatments like steroid creams, and if so, did they help at all? Also, does anyone else in your household have a similar itchy rash right now?
I haven't tried any steroid creams yet, just some regular lotion that doesn't seem to do much for the itching. No one else at home has anything like this; it's just me dealing with it.

Does the itching worsen at night or interfere with your sleep, and have you noticed any similar dryness or rashes behind your knees? I would also like to rule out other possibilities with a simple skin scraping.

REQUEST TEST: KOH_Prep
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

Does anyone in your family suffer from asthma, hay fever, or chronic skin conditions like this? Also, do you find that your skin is generally dry all over, even in areas where you don't have the rash?
My mom mentioned she had some hay fever issues when she was younger, but I'm not sure about anyone else. My skin does tend to feel pretty dry overall, especially during the winter months.
Since you mentioned your skin feels dry all over, have you noticed any small, rough bumps on your upper arms or thighs that feel like sandpaper? I would like to perform one final check

I do have some of those tiny, rough bumps on the backs of my arms, almost like permanent goosebumps. They don't really itch like the rash does, but they definitely make my skin feel sandpaper-y. Please, go ahead with whatever check you need to do.

Have you ever experienced any wheezing or shortness of breath, perhaps during exercise or certain seasons? I would also like to check a specific lab value to see if your immune system is reacting to allergies.

REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgE
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

Based on the location of the rash in your elbow folds, your childhood history, and the presence of rough bumps on your arms, I have a clear picture of your condition. Thank you for answering my questions
Of course, doctor. What do you think is causing this, and is there something I can do to finally stop this itching? I'm really hoping for some relief since it's been bothering me for so many months.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Atopic Dermatitis
